title: Absolute September ENSO gave no clear added Pacific dry-area forecast gain in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether absolute September Nino 3.4 improves forecasts of the October-December low-rain area in 10 S-10 N, 120 E-280 E. The target is the cosine-area fraction below each GPCP V2.3 cell's 20th percentile from 1979-1999. Each fit used earlier years only. The baseline used signed September Nino 3.4, recent dry area and trend. The added term reduced mean squared error by 15.7% across 26 years in 2000-2025. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -26.1% to +44.5%, so there was no clear added gain. RMSE fell from 8.10 to 7.44 area percentage points. Fixed checks gave positive point gains but did not remove the wide primary uncertainty. This is a revised-data forecast test, not a test of physical cause or land water supply. A short record, one coarse product, a fixed anomaly reference and conditional intervals limit inference. The package gives code, losses, draws, source hashes, a figure and an independent numerical check. Raw data and observation tables remain external and can be regenerated into separate scratch.

display.caption: Observed low-rain area, forecasts, and annual error reduction for a Pacific box. The primary added absolute-ENSO term gives no clear gain. GPCP V2.3 data provided by NOAA PSL. Copyright (2026) GPCP.
